## Vulcano plots highlight the amount of interesting proteins



# Data wrangling

The new data was loaded. To better work with the data, the only the entries for TSB vs. SN were used. To plot the data in a volcano plot, an additional variable is added.
```{r}
#import needed libraries
library(tidyverse)

#get our data in
suppressWarnings(
protein_abundances <- readxl::read_excel("/home/BIO144_FS26/Users/samlut/Research cycles in omics/bio253-je2-proteomics/bio253-je2-proteomics/data/raw/total/DE_total.xlsx", sheet = "diff_exp_analysis")
)


#take only data of contrast TSB vs SN:
protein_abundances_TSB_SN <- protein_abundances |> filter(contrast == "TSB_vs_SN")

#add axis of vulcan plot to dataset (-log10_FDR) 
protein_abundances_TSB_SN <- protein_abundances_TSB_SN |> mutate(neg__log10_FDR = -log10(FDR))


```


The entries have to be classified based on their differential expression and the FDR value. Because the cutoff is biologically arbitrary, we used a common cutoff in the field of a differential expression of at least twice or a half. For a broader array of possible proteins the FDR of 0.1 was chosen as the cutoff.

For better presentation in the plot, the direction of the differential expression was changed, such that upregulation is positive and downregulation is negative. 
```{r}
#add classification of cutoff 
protein_abundances_TSB_SN <- protein_abundances_TSB_SN |> mutate(regulation = case_when(
  -diff <= log2(1/2) & neg__log10_FDR >= 1 ~ "down",
  -diff >= log2(2) & neg__log10_FDR >= 1~ "up",
  .default = "n.s."
))

```



## Plotting

```{r}
#make color labels
manual_colors = c(
  "down" = "darkblue",
  "up" = "magenta",
  "n.s" = "lightgrey"
)

#create vulcano plot
a <- ggplot(data = protein_abundances_TSB_SN, aes(x = -diff, y = neg__log10_FDR, col = regulation)) +
  geom_point() +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 1, col = "gray", linetype = "dashed") +
  geom_vline(xintercept = log2(1/2), col = "gray", linetype = "dashed") +
  geom_vline(xintercept = log2(2), col = "gray", linetype = "dashed") +
  ggtitle("Change in protein regulation TSB vs. SN") +
  xlab("-log2_FC (TSB / PASN)") +
  ylab("-log10_FDR") +
  scale_color_manual(values = manual_colors)


plotly::ggplotly(a)


```
